questions.q:
With reference to the history of defections in India, consider the following statements:
1. About 45 State governments rose and fell because of defections between 1977 and 1980.
2. The Y.B. Chavan Committee defined defection as voluntarily giving up allegiance to the party on whose symbol a legislator was elected, unless the act followed a party decision.
3. In the United Kingdom, a Member of Parliament who defies the party whip loses the seat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The wave of about 45 government collapses came in 1967-71, after the 1967 elections ended one-party dominance in several States; that period is called the era of instability. The Chavan Committee of 1969 was the first systematic study. The United Kingdom, like the United States and Canada, has no anti-defection law: members who defy the whip keep their seats and face only internal party discipline.

questions.q: Article 361B, inserted along with Articles 75(1B) and 164(1B) by the Constitution (Ninety-first Amendment) Act, 2003, provides that a member disqualified under the Tenth Schedule shall also be disqualified from
o: being chosen as a member of either House of Parliament for six years
contesting the next general election to the House concerned
holding any remunerative political post until re-elected or until the term of the House expires
voting in an election to the office of President
questions.e: The 91st Amendment tried to remove the rewards of defection. Articles 75(1B) and 164(1B) bar a disqualified defector from being appointed a Minister, and Article 361B extends the bar to remunerative political posts, in each case until the member is re-elected or the term ends. The amendment did not impose a six-year bar or stop the person from contesting again; in fact re-election lifts the bar. The same amendment deleted the one-third split exception.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 5; text of Article 361B is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs on the anti-defection law:
Case : What the Supreme Court held
1. Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu : The presiding officer acts as a tribunal and the decision is open to judicial review
2. Ravi S. Naik v. Union of India : A formal resignation from the party is necessary to show that membership was voluntarily given up
3. Nabam Rebia v. Deputy Speaker : A Speaker facing a notice for removal should not decide disqualification petitions
4. Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur : Disqualification petitions should ordinarily be decided within three months
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld the Tenth Schedule but treated the Speaker as a tribunal whose order is reviewable, judicial review being part of the basic structure. Nabam Rebia (2016) and Keisham Meghachandra (2020) deal with a Speaker under a removal notice and with the three-month outer limit. Pair 2 is wrong: Ravi Naik (1994) held that giving up membership can be inferred from conduct and needs no formal resignation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Tenth Schedule was inserted in the Constitution by the Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act.
Statement-II: The anti-defection law was enacted in 1985, when Rajiv Gandhi was Prime Minister.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. The Tenth Schedule was inserted by the Fifty-second Amendment in 1985 under Rajiv Gandhi. The Sixty-first Amendment of 1988 lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years. The Ninety-first Amendment of 2003 later deleted the split exception and barred defectors from ministerial office and remunerative political posts.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 4-5; the 61st Amendment is static

questions.q:
In which of the following countries can a legislator lose the seat for defying the party whip, according to the comparative position noted in the 2026 debate on defections?
1. Pakistan
2. Bangladesh
3. Canada
4. Zimbabwe
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Guyana, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe provide for disqualification of members who defy the party whip. The United Kingdom, the United States and Canada have no anti-defection law: a member who votes against the party keeps the seat and is dealt with through internal party discipline. Canada is therefore the odd one out in the list.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Supreme Court's judgment in Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu
2. Report of the Y.B. Chavan Committee on Defections
3. Deletion of the 'split' exception from the Tenth Schedule
4. Insertion of the Tenth Schedule in the Constitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Chavan Committee (1969) was the first systematic study of defections and followed the instability of 1967-71, when about 45 State governments rose and fell. The Tenth Schedule came in 1985 through the 52nd Amendment under Rajiv Gandhi. Kihoto Hollohan (1992) upheld it subject to judicial review, and the 91st Amendment of 2003 removed the split exception.

questions.q: The expression 'Aya Ram, Gaya Ram', used for frequent floor-crossing by legislators, originated from an episode of 1967 involving a legislator of
questions.e: The phrase goes back to a Haryana MLA who changed parties three times in a single day in 1967, soon after the general elections that ended one-party dominance in several States. The period 1967-71 is called the era of instability because defections for office or money brought down a large number of State governments. This background led to the Y.B. Chavan Committee and, much later, to the Tenth Schedule.

questions.q:
With reference to Prison Statistics India 2024, consider the following statements:
1. The national occupancy rate of prisons rose to its highest level in a decade.
2. Undertrials formed close to three-fourths of all inmates.
3. The share of convicts among inmates has risen steadily since 2016.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Occupancy at the end of 2024 was 112.7 per cent, the lowest in a decade, with about 5.11 lakh inmates against a capacity of 4.53 lakh, so statement 1 is wrong. Undertrials were about 73 per cent, below the 2021 peak of about 77 per cent. Statement 3 is also wrong: the share of convicts fell from about 32 per cent in 2016 to 26.6 per cent in 2024.

questions.q:
With reference to State-wise prison occupancy in Prison Statistics India 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Bihar recorded the highest occupancy rate among States and Union Territories.
2. Occupancy in Jammu and Kashmir rose from below capacity in 2015 to nearly one and a half times capacity in 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Delhi had the highest occupancy, 194 per cent in 2024 after 200 per cent in 2023. Bihar, with Delhi, stands out for a different reason: undertrials are over 87 per cent of its inmates. Jammu and Kashmir moved from 78 per cent in 2015 to about 148 per cent, while Chhattisgarh moved the other way, from 234 per cent to 127.6 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Subject
1. State of Andhra Pradesh v. Challa Ramkrishna Reddy : A prisoner retains all fundamental rights except those curtailed by the Constitution
2. Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar : Speedy trial as part of Article 21
3. D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal : Caste-based allotment of work in prison manuals
4. Sukanya Shantha v. Union of India : Guidelines to be followed at the time of arrest and detention
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The subjects of the last two have been interchanged. D.K. Basu (1996) laid down the arrest and detention safeguards meant to prevent custodial torture. Sukanya Shantha (2024) struck down prison-manual rules that gave cleaning work to the so-called lower castes and cooking to others, as contrary to Articles 14, 15, 17 and 21.

questions.q: In Suhas Chakma v. Union of India (2026), a case arising from chronic congestion in jails, the Supreme Court issued nationwide directions mainly on
o: release of undertrials who have served half the maximum sentence
payment of minimum wages to convict labour
expansion and uniform governance of open correctional institutions
questions.e: The Court used the case to push open correctional institutions, asking that they be expanded and run on uniform lines across States, as one way of easing overcrowded closed prisons. Open prisons hold selected convicts with minimal security and allow them to work, and are listed among the structural reforms along with psychiatric support and faster trials. The other options are real debates in prison reform but were not the focus of this ruling.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Model Prisons Act, 2023 prepared by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs does not by itself replace the Prisons Act, 1894 in a State.
Statement-II: 'Prisons' is a subject in the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. Prisons and the persons detained in them, like the police, fall in the State List, so only a State legislature can make the governing law. The Centre can circulate a model statute for States to adopt. The 2023 model law, which stresses rehabilitation and modernisation, therefore takes effect in a State only when that State enacts it in place of the colonial 1894 Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 17-18; Entry 4, List II is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on the legal protections available to prisoners:
1. Article 20(2) protects a person from being prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once.
2. Article 22 gives an arrested person the right to consult a legal practitioner of his choice.
3. Free legal aid under Article 39A is a fundamental right enforceable under Article 32.
4. The Prisons Act, 1894 provides for keeping convicts and undertrials separately.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Double jeopardy is in Article 20(2), and Article 22 covers the right to be told the grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer. The 1894 Act requires separation of convicts from undertrials, civil from criminal prisoners and women from men. Statement 3 is wrong as framed: Article 39A is a Directive Principle. Legal aid is given effect through the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 and has been read into Article 21 by the courts.

questions.q:
With reference to prison reform proposals discussed in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. At present, children are allowed to stay with their imprisoned mothers up to the age of six years.
2. Electronic tracking devices for undertrials, as an aid to release on bail, have been tried out in Odisha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The suggestion is to raise the age up to which a child may stay with the mother in prison from six to twelve years and to give pregnant women the option of giving birth outside prison. Bracelet or anklet trackers were tested in Odisha and are proposed only with the inmate's consent. Other proposals are State-level funds to pay fines and bail for poor prisoners and a rule that no post stays vacant beyond three months.

questions.q: In June 2026 the Bombay High Court dealt with the meaning of 'workplace' under the law on sexual harassment of women at the workplace. The Court held that
o: a shared autorickshaw used for commuting is not a workplace unless the transport is provided by the employer
any public transport used for commuting to work is a workplace
a workplace is confined to premises owned or controlled by the employer
harassment during a commute can be examined only by the Local Committee
questions.e: The Act's definition covers any place visited by the employee arising out of or in the course of employment, including transport provided by the employer for the journey. On this wording the Court held that a privately hired shared autorickshaw falls outside, while employer-arranged transport is inside. The definition is still wider than the employer's premises: it also covers homes where domestic workers are employed, and courts have extended it to digital platforms.

questions.q:
Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, which of the following fall within the meaning of 'workplace'?
1. A dwelling house in which a domestic worker is employed
2. A stadium or sports complex used for training, even if it is not residential
3. An enterprise in the unorganised sector that employs fewer than ten workers
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three are covered. Section 2(o) lists government bodies, private-sector organisations, hospitals and nursing homes, sports institutes and venues whether residential or not, places visited in the course of employment, and a dwelling place or house. The unorganised sector is defined for the Act as enterprises owned by individuals or self-employed workers with fewer than ten workers, and it is expressly included rather than exempted.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the judicial reading of the law on sexual harassment at the workplace is not correct?
o: Courts have treated messaging and social-media platforms as part of the workplace even when the persons involved are in different places.
The Delhi High Court has held that 'workplace' should not be given a narrow meaning and may include atypical spaces.
The Vishaka guidelines rested on Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(g) and 21 of the Constitution.
Sexual harassment under the law is confined to physical acts and does not extend to verbal or non-verbal conduct.
questions.e: Harassment is not limited to physical contact; the Delhi High Court in the Sanchayani Sharma line of reasoning treated verbal and non-verbal conduct as covered. The Rajasthan High Court in Sanjeev Mishra and the Delhi High Court in Jahid Ali brought digital platforms and social media within the workplace, and Saurabh Kumar Mallick rejected a narrow reading. Vishaka read the right to a safe working environment into equality, the freedom to practise a profession and the right to life.

questions.q: A woman working in an establishment that has fewer than ten workers, and therefore has no Internal Committee, wishes to complain of sexual harassment under the 2013 Act. Her complaint lies to the
o: Judicial Magistrate of the first class
Local Committee constituted by the District Officer
questions.e: Every employer with ten or more workers must set up an Internal Committee. For smaller establishments, and for complaints against the employer himself, the District Officer constitutes a Local Committee in each district. This matters for domestic workers and the unorganised sector, where the difficulty of small units in forming committees is one of the gaps noted in the working of the Act. Women's commissions and courts are not the forum of first complaint under this law.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 44; Local Committee provision is static

questions.q:
Which of the following changes were made by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951?
1. Creation of the Ninth Schedule
2. Insertion of clause (4) in Article 15
3. Amendment of the provisions on summoning, prorogation and dissolution of the Houses
4. Insertion of Article 31C
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Amendment created the Ninth Schedule along with Articles 31A and 31B, inserted Article 15(4) after the Champakam Dorairajan ruling, and amended Articles 85, 87, 174 and 176 to give more flexibility over sessions, prorogation and dissolution. Article 31C, which protects laws giving effect to Article 39(b) and (c), was inserted twenty years later by the Twenty-fifth Amendment of 1971.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 45; Article 31C is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951:
Judgment : Its connection with the Amendment
1. Romesh Thapar v. State of Madras : Led to widening of the grounds of restriction on free speech
2. State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan : Led to the creation of the Ninth Schedule
3. Shankari Prasad v. Union of India : Struck down the Amendment as beyond the amending power
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Romesh Thapar struck down a public-order ban on a journal and led to wider grounds in Article 19(2). Champakam Dorairajan struck down the Communal G.O. on admissions and led to Article 15(4); the Ninth Schedule answered High Court rulings on zamindari abolition. In Shankari Prasad (1951) the Court upheld the First Amendment.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 45; Shankari Prasad is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A law placed in the Ninth Schedule could not, for a long time, be struck down for violating a fundamental right.
Statement-II: Article 31B, inserted by the Forty-second Amendment, declares that laws specified in the Ninth Schedule shall not be void for inconsistency with any provision of Part III.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule were inserted by the First Amendment of 1951 to save zamindari-abolition laws. The Schedule later held a few hundred laws, many unrelated to land reform. In I.R. Coelho (2007) the Court held that laws added after 24 April 1973 can be tested against the basic structure.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 45-46; I.R. Coelho is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, consider the following statements:
1. It was passed by the first Lok Sabha after the general elections of 1951-52.
2. It inserted Article 15(4) to enable reservation in promotions in public employment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The Amendment was enacted in June 1951 by the Provisional Parliament, before the first general elections, about fifteen months after the Constitution came into force. Article 15(4) enables special provisions for backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Tribes and arose from a ruling on admissions; reservation in promotion is Article 16(4A), added in 1995.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 44-45; Article 16(4A) is static

questions.q: Article 31A, one of the provisions inserted by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, protects
o: laws listed in the Ninth Schedule from challenge on any ground
laws giving effect to the Directive Principles in Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Article 14
laws providing for acquisition of estates and similar agrarian measures from challenge under Articles 14 and 19
a person from being deprived of property except by authority of law
questions.e: Article 31A saves certain classes of laws, beginning with the acquisition of estates, from attack under Articles 14 and 19; it was meant to protect zamindari abolition. Protection of laws listed in the Ninth Schedule comes from Article 31B. Protection of laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) is Article 31C, added in 1971. The guarantee against deprivation of property without authority of law is now Article 300A, a constitutional and not a fundamental right.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 45-46; Articles 31C and 300A are static

questions.q:
With reference to the temporary blocking of the messaging platform Telegram in India in June 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The blocking order was issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre.
2. The provision invoked permits blocking of online content only on the ground of defamation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The block, in force until 22 June 2026, was ordered by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology under Section 69A of the IT Act at the NTA's request; the I4C acted against channels and bots. Section 69A's grounds are sovereignty and integrity, defence, security of the State, friendly relations, public order and preventing incitement; defamation is not one of them.

questions.q: Along with the block of June 2026, Telegram was asked to suspend the editing of messages in India until 30 June 2026. The misuse that this step was meant to prevent was that
o: edited posts were automatically forwarded to all subscribers of linked channels
edited messages could not be traced by the platform to the original sender
editing allowed users to bypass end-to-end encryption and read private chats
channel administrators replaced old posts with the actual question paper after the examination, so that the unchanged time-stamp suggested a leak before the examination
questions.e: Telegram lets a post be edited while keeping its original time-stamp. Fraudulent channels took money for a 'leaked' paper, then after the examination edited an earlier post to insert the real paper and used the old time-stamp as proof of a prior leak. The NTA maintained that no genuine re-examination paper had leaked. The restriction is notable as regulation aimed at a single feature of a platform, not only at content.

questions.q: The blocking of online platforms under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 has been criticised for opacity. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015), the Supreme Court
o: struck down Section 69A along with Section 66A
upheld Section 66A but read down Section 69A
struck down Section 66A but upheld Section 69A and the blocking rules
held that only a High Court may order the blocking of a website
questions.e: Shreya Singhal invalidated Section 66A for vagueness and overbreadth but upheld Section 69A, noting that blocking is confined to grounds tied to Article 19(2), that reasons must be recorded in writing and that the blocking rules provide a procedure. Critics point out that orders are still made without prior judicial scrutiny and are rarely disclosed, which is the due-process concern raised again by the platform-wide Telegram block.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 51-52; Shreya Singhal is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Entity : Description
1. National Testing Agency : Functions under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2. Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre : Functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
3. Telegram : Cloud-based messaging service founded in 2013 by Pavel Durov
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 3 is correct. The National Testing Agency, which conducts NEET-UG, is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Education. The I4C is a body of the Ministry of Home Affairs; the blocking power under Section 69A is exercised by the electronics and IT ministry. Telegram was founded in 2013 by Pavel Durov.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 50-51; I4C's ministry is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's decision in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India (2026) on the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, consider the following statements:
1. The Court traced the Commission's power to conduct the revision to Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
2. The Court held that the Commission may declare a person to be a non-citizen after a hearing.
3. Where doubt about a person's citizenship persists, the final determination lies with the Election Commission itself.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Court drew a line between eligibility for the roll and citizenship status: the Commission only decides whether the material justifies inclusion and cannot declare anyone a non-citizen, so statement 2 is wrong. Where doubt persists, the matter goes to the Central Government, which alone decides citizenship under the Citizenship Act, 1955, so statement 3 is wrong as well.

questions.q: Section 16 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, relied on in the litigation over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, deals with
o: the requirement of ordinary residence in a constituency
the preparation and revision of electoral rolls
disqualifications for registration in an electoral roll, including not being a citizen of India
the right to vote at an election
questions.e: Section 16 disqualifies from registration a person who is not a citizen of India, is of unsound mind as declared by a court, or is disqualified for corrupt practices. Because the statute itself bars non-citizens, the Court accepted that the Commission may examine citizenship for roll purposes. Ordinary residence is in Section 19 and revision of rolls in Section 21 of the same Act, while the right to vote is in Section 62 of the 1951 Act.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 55; other sections are static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The right to vote in India has been treated as a statutory right and not as a fundamental right.
Statement-II: In its 2026 ruling on the Special Intensive Revision, the Supreme Court held that the Election Commission may examine citizenship only for the purpose of deciding eligibility for the electoral roll.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the second does not explain the first. The statutory character of the right to vote comes from the fact that it is conferred by election law, even though Article 326 lays down adult suffrage. The second statement records a separate holding on the limits of the Commission's inquiry. The Court also said that verification must satisfy natural justice and Article 14 because exclusion affects identity and dignity.

questions.q: Critics of large-scale verification of voters point to the experience of 'D-Voters' in Assam. Persons marked as doubtful voters during the 1997 revision of rolls had their cases referred to
o: the Election Commission of India for final decision
the Gauhati High Court's election bench
questions.e: In the 1997 revision in Assam many persons were marked 'D', or doubtful, and their cases went to Foreigners Tribunals. Cases stayed pending for decades, and those marked lost access to welfare and lived with stigma and legal uncertainty. The concern is that a nationwide exercise could reproduce this on a larger scale, which is why time-bound determination of referred cases is among the safeguards suggested.

questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's 2026 ruling on the taxation of online gaming, consider the following statements:
1. Goods and Services Tax at 28 per cent applies to the full value of the stakes and not merely to the platform's fee.
2. The changes recommended by the GST Council in August 2023 were treated as clarificatory and therefore applicable to earlier periods as well.
3. The distinction between games of skill and games of chance was held to be irrelevant for GST once money is staked on an uncertain outcome.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The industry wanted the tax confined to the platform's retained share, the 'rake', and relied on the skill-chance distinction. The Court held that the CGST Act already covered actionable claims in betting and gambling, that the 2023 changes only standardised the position, and that demands for periods before October 2023 were valid. The demands raised by the tax intelligence wing run into several lakh crore rupees.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Entry in the Seventh Schedule : Subject
1. Entry 34, List II : Betting and gambling
2. Entry 2, List II : Public order
3. Entry 52, List I : Industries whose control by the Union is declared by Parliament to be expedient in the public interest
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. The Supreme Court upheld State prohibitions on real-money gaming by relying on Entry 34 and on public order, which is Entry 1 of the State List; Entry 2 is police. Entry 52 of the Union List is the basis cited for the central Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025. Since the Court has reaffirmed betting as a State subject, Parliament's competence for that Act may be tested.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 58-59; Entry 2 is static

questions.q: The doctrine of res extra commercium, applied by the Supreme Court in 2026 to betting and gambling, means that such activities
o: lie outside legitimate trade and so cannot claim the constitutional protection given to trade and business
are regulated by international commercial law
must be carried on only by the State
can be taxed only by the Union
questions.e: The phrase means 'a thing outside commerce'. An activity so classified is treated as inherently harmful, so those who carry it on cannot invoke the freedom of trade or business against a prohibition. The Court reasoned that even a game of skill takes on the character of wagering once money is staked, which brings it within the States' power over betting and gambling. The doctrine says nothing about which government may tax it.

questions.q: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, which one of the following is prohibited?
o: Online games played for money stakes
Online social games played without stakes
questions.e: The 2025 Act bans online real-money gaming altogether, on the reasoning that digital wallets and crypto-assets on such platforms were being used for money laundering and posed a security risk. E-sports, educational games and social games are kept out of the ban. With the retrospective tax demands also upheld, companies have moved abroad or shifted to social gaming and fintech, and insolvencies are expected.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court did not accept the claim that fantasy sports platforms, being predominantly games of skill, are beyond State laws that prohibit betting.
Statement-II: According to the Court, staking money on an outcome that cannot be predicted with certainty gives the activity the character of wagering, whatever skill it may involve.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second gives the Court's reason. In fantasy sports users assemble virtual teams of real players and score on actual match statistics. The Court noted that even sophisticated models cannot forecast results with certainty and that smartphones and digital payments have turned every phone into a virtual gambling house. On that footing the Tamil Nadu and Karnataka laws of 2021, earlier struck down by their High Courts, were upheld.

questions.q: The Directorate General of GST Intelligence, which issued tax demand notices to online gaming companies, functions under the
o: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
questions.e: The DGGI is the intelligence and investigation wing for indirect taxes under the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs in the Department of Revenue. It raised demands on gaming firms for periods both before and after the October 2023 change in the law. The GST Council only recommends rates and rules, the GSTN runs the technology platform, and the Enforcement Directorate deals with money laundering and foreign-exchange violations.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 57; DGGI's parent body is static

questions.q:
With reference to the litigation on online gaming that the Supreme Court decided in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Laws of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka that criminalised betting on online games had earlier been struck down by their High Courts.
2. The Bombay and Karnataka High Courts had earlier upheld the tax demands by treating online gaming transactions as actionable claims.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The two States' 2021 laws were struck down by the Madras and Karnataka High Courts and the States appealed, citing their power over betting and gambling. On the tax side the High Courts had ruled for the companies: they held that the transactions were not actionable claims and quashed the proceedings. The Union appealed, and the Supreme Court reversed both lines of decisions.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Judge : Associated fact
1. H.R. Khanna : Author of the autobiography 'Neither Roses Nor Thorns'
2. M.H. Beg : Appointed Chief Justice of India in supersession of Justice H.R. Khanna
3. D.Y. Chandrachud : Fiftieth Chief Justice of India
4. Ruth Bader Ginsburg : Judge of the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Justice Khanna, the lone dissenter in ADM Jabalpur (1976), was passed over the next year in favour of Justice Beg, who had been in the majority, and resigned. Justice Chandrachud retired as the fiftieth Chief Justice in November 2024. Pair 4 is wrong: Justice Ginsburg sat on the Supreme Court of the United States. The English judge cited in the 2026 debate on court vacations is Lord Denning.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Justice H.R. Khanna was appointed Chief Justice of India soon after his dissent in ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976).
Statement-II: In K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), the Supreme Court expressly overruled the majority view in ADM Jabalpur.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. Justice Khanna, the lone dissenter, was superseded the next year by Justice M.H. Beg, who had been in the majority, and he resigned. His view that the right to life does not depend on Article 21 alone was vindicated when the nine-judge Bench in the privacy case overruled the majority in 2017.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 60; Puttaswamy is static

questions.q: The long summer recess of the higher judiciary is often traced to the convenience of the European judges of the Federal Court of India. The Federal Court was set up under the
questions.e: The Federal Court was created by the Government of India Act, 1935 and began sitting in Delhi in 1937; the Supreme Court replaced it in January 1950. The summer break is said to have begun because its European judges found the Indian summer too hot, and the winter break was for Christmas. The case made in 2026 is that judges now use these breaks to write reserved judgments and read records, so they are working periods.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 59; the 1935 Act is static
